cases.sentence: — У каждого своя ___, — продолжал князь Андрей.

cases.translation: “Everyone has his Achilles’ heel,” continued Prince Andréy. “Fancy, with his powerful mind, indulging in such nonsense!”

cases.sentence: Князь остановился; из-под висячих ___ оживленные, блестящие, строгие глаза оглядели всех и остановились на молодой княгине.
cases.explain: «густых бровей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Princess Márya could not understand the boldness of her brother’s criticism and was about to reply, when the expected footsteps were heard coming from the study. The prince walked in quickly and jauntily as was his wont, as if intentionally contrasting the briskness of his manners with the strict formality of his house. At that moment the great clock struck two and another with a shrill tone joined in from the drawing room. The prince stood still; his lively glittering eyes from under their thick, bushy eyebrows sternly scanned all present and rested on the little princess. She felt, as courtiers do when the Tsar enters, the sensation of fear and respect which the old man inspired in all around him. He stroked her hair and then patted her awkwardly on the back of her neck.

cases.sentence: ___ не слыхала или не хотела слышать его слов.
cases.explain: «Маленькая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The little princess did not, or did not wish to, hear his words. She was silent and seemed confused. The prince asked her about her father, and she began to smile and talk. He asked about mutual acquaintances, and she became still more animated and chattered away giving him greetings from various people and retelling the town gossip.

cases.sentence: Как мне князь Андрей (он всегда так называл сына в ___) порассказал, какие на него силы собираются!
cases.explain: «третьем лице» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Well, Mikháil Ivánovich, our Buonaparte will be having a bad time of it. Prince Andréy” (he always spoke thus of his son) “has been telling me what forces are being collected against him! While you and I never thought much of him.”

cases.sentence: И разговор зашел опять о войне, о Бонапарте и ___ и государственных людях.
cases.explain: «нынешних генералах» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: And the conversation again turned on the war, on Bonaparte, and the generals and statesmen of the day. The old prince seemed convinced not only that all the men of the day were mere babies who did not know the A.B.C. of war or of politics, and that Bonaparte was an insignificant little Frenchy, successful only because there were no longer any Potëmkins or Suvórovs left to oppose him; but he was also convinced that there were no political difficulties in Europe and no real war, but only a sort of puppet show at which the men of the day were playing, pretending to do something real. Prince Andréy gaily bore with his father’s ridicule of the new men, and drew him on and listened to him with evident pleasure.
